name: Garlicky Chickpea & Spinach Sauté
pitch: This simple Mediterranean-style skillet comes together in minutes and tastes like you put in way more effort than you did.
steps: Heat a generous drizzle of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 3–4 minced garlic cloves and cook for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Add your drained, rinsed chickpeas and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of cumin or paprika if you have it. Cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they get a little golden.

Toss in the spinach a few big handfuls at a time, stirring until wilted — just 2–3 minutes. Finish with a splash of vinegar or a squeeze of lemon juice if you have one, and taste for seasoning. Serve as-is or over rice or toast.

name: Spiced Chickpea & Spinach Curry
pitch: A cozy, warming curry that's incredibly satisfying — just note you'll want a can of coconut milk or diced tomatoes to make the sauce, which you may not have on hand.
steps: Heat oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté 3 cloves of minced garlic for 1 minute, then add 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp paprika (or whatever warm spices you have). Stir for 30 seconds.
Add your drained chickpeas and one can of diced tomatoes (or coconut milk). Stir everything together, bring to a simmer, and let it cook for 10–12 minutes so the flavors meld.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 2–3 minutes. Season well with salt and pepper. Serve over rice or with bread for dipping — simple but really comforting.
toolSuggestion: Medium saucepan or pot with a lid

name: Crispy Chickpea & Spinach Rice Bowl
pitch: Roasting the chickpeas gives them an addictive crunch that makes this bowl feel way more special than its short ingredient list suggests.
steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C). Pat your drained chickpeas very dry with a paper towel — this is the key to crispiness! Toss them with oil, salt, pepper, and any spice you like (smoked paprika is great). Spread on a baking sheet and roast for 20–25 minutes, shaking once halfway through.

While the chickpeas roast, cook rice according to package directions. In the last few minutes, toss your spinach into the rice pot with a splash of water and put the lid back on — it'll steam and wilt right in there.
Scoop rice and spinach into bowls, top with the crispy chickpeas, and drizzle with a little soy sauce or a splash of vinegar for brightness. It's simple but satisfying.
